quotes.text: Learn how to accept the Multibanco payment method.

old_evidence.text: Customers use these voucher details to make a payment outside your checkout flow through online banking or from an ATM.
The PaymentIntent remains in the `processing` status for a maximum buffer period of 4 days
When you successfully reconfirm a PaymentIntent in status `requires_action`, Stripe creates new voucher instructions and a new `hosted_voucher_url`.

findings: The 2026-11-07 canonical response contains only purpose and links to Checkout, Direct API, iOS, and Android (new raw 1–17). Those reported routes match the four 2026-05-07 detailed headings and query variants (old raw 8–10, 193–195, 614–616, 895–897). The diff on line 1167 joins the last removed line and first added route because of the ending formatting; inspect the exact old raw 1164–1166 and new raw 13–17 for the boundary.

The historical guide covers Portuguese customers paying a EUR voucher via online banking or ATM and describes the Europe/US business scope. Checkout has one-time EUR line items in payment mode, with dynamic presentation and a manual enablement path. Direct API and both mobile examples instead create an amount-and-EUR PaymentIntent on the server and use the client secret for browser or mobile confirmation. The browser uses `stripe.confirmMultibancoPayment` or optional server confirmation; iOS and Android use separate SDK APIs (old raw 12–55, 109–127, 193–238, 307–392, 715–805 and 971–1078).

Baseline weaknesses in the summary include vague Boleto/Konbini event shorthand, ambiguous integration count and an unconditional four-day lifecycle after expiry. Old raw 125–127, 168–182, 383–385, 543–556, 778–805 and 1034–1078 identify the precise fulfillment boundary, maximum processing time, separate client results and the consequence of reconfirmation (source 13–34).
historical_claims_to_preserve: The 2026-05-07 guide describes an entity/reference voucher paid outside checkout via online banking or ATM, applicable to Portuguese customers and Europe/US businesses, with bank transfers sometimes delaying confirmation several days, especially over weekends. Checkout supports one-time EUR items in payment mode, excluding setup and subscription modes (old raw 18–41).

Hosted and full embedded Checkout examples use their own session parameters, and the voucher flow routes to `hosted_voucher_url`. Direct API ordinarily displays a voucher modal via Stripe.js or allows `handleActions: false`; optional server confirmation creates a PaymentMethod from the supplied billing email and can redirect using the PaymentIntent’s `next_action`. iOS and Android confirm via their SDK and display a webview. Preserve server/client, Checkout Session/PaymentIntent/PaymentMethod, and UI boundaries (old raw 51–115, 307–385, 387–518, 761–805 and 1017–1078).

Checkout form completion creates a voucher; fulfillment follows `checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded`. Its asynchronous failure example covers expiry or other failure. Direct API and mobile treat `payment_intent.requires_action` or a client display result as voucher issuance and `payment_intent.succeeded` as the paid signal (old raw 115–127, 543–556, 778–805, 824–837, 1034–1078 and 1097–1110).

The documented May lifecycle gives 7 days to pay, then a processing window of up to 4 days for notification of an already initiated transfer. If payment does not complete within it, the intent returns to `requires_payment_method`. Stripe initiates a refund for funds received after the buffer or against a canceled voucher. Pending cancellation invalidates the old instructions, and successful reconfirmation of a `requires_action` intent generates replacement instructions and hosted URL that must be supplied to the customer. The 11-day `fill_never` flow is a sandbox scenario (old raw 164–182, 590–608, 871–889 and 1144–1162).
conflicts: Source 19 labels its unnamed group as three async webhook events. Checkout’s table distinguishes ordinary `checkout.session.completed` for voucher creation from asynchronous success/failure (old raw 119–127). Checkout can also emit `payment_intent.requires_action` on successful voucher creation (old raw 109–115). Direct API and mobile instead identify PaymentIntent events and client display callbacks (old raw 383–385, 543–556, 791–805 and 1062–1078).

Source 23–26 and voucher concept 93 imply a fixed or unconditional processing-to-failure progression and completed refund. The old text describes up to four days, a conditional failure path, and initiation of the refund process for late funds (old raw 168–182 and 1148–1162). Source 32 omits that successful reconfirmation creates new instructions and URL requiring customer delivery.

Voucher concept 10 and 27 frame payment as in-person cash only, while its own Multibanco-specific line 79 and old raw 18–22 document online banking as well as ATM payment. Its line 93 should qualify the hosted redirect to its described routes and distinguish the Direct API modal and mobile webview. The concept’s Billing `send_invoice` entry at lines 14–19 and 89 concerns a separate product path from the old acceptance guide’s one-time Checkout payment mode (old raw 24–41).
unresolved_questions: The linked November variants were not part of the captured evidence. Their present-day contents and compatibility, merchant eligibility, account configuration, live outcome and refund timing remain unverified.

findings: Replace the ambiguous integration count in source 13–19 with Checkout, Direct API, and the separate iOS/Android SDK paths. Preserve Checkout payment mode with one-time same-currency EUR items, the business/customer scope, dynamic presentation and manual enablement, and keep Checkout Session events separate from PaymentIntent status and mobile display results (old raw 12–55, 109–127, 383–385, 543–556, 778–805 and 1034–1078).

Scope hosted voucher redirect to Checkout and the optional Direct API server route. The client route has a default modal and optional manual rendering, while the mobile examples use webviews. The historical manual voucher requires entity, reference, expiry date, amount and EUR (source 13–30; old raw 109–115, 350–383, 387–518, 778–805 and 1034–1078).

In source 23–34, describe notification processing as up to 4 days after expiry, make `requires_payment_method` conditional on failure to complete, and say Stripe initiates a refund if late or canceled-voucher funds arrive. Keep replacement instructions after reconfirmation, and label `fill_never` as a sandbox scenario. Link the dated detailed and November navigation captures separately and add a source route back to the voucher concept (old raw 146–182; new raw 5–17; voucher concept 93 and 121).
conflicts: The shorthand `same 3 async webhook events` at source 19 obscures issuance versus paid state and mixes distinct event families. Old raw 115–127 and 543–556 specify voucher creation, pending and success boundaries.

The fixed-looking timing and auto-refund wording in source 23–32 and the voucher concept line 93 overstate old raw 168–182. The voucher concept’s general cash-only language at 10 and 27 conflicts with the dated online banking route in old raw 18–22 and its own line 79.
source_assessments.reason: The November capture is navigation only. The baseline source needs explicit fulfillment and processing boundaries, and a warning about replacement voucher instructions, to answer implementation queries without conflating object state, UI outcome and receipt of funds.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/multibanco/accept-a-payment, new raw lines 5-17 give the purpose and links to Checkout, Direct API, iOS and Android without capturing the variant instructions. The 2026-05-07 detailed guide says Portuguese customers receive an entity/reference voucher and pay outside checkout through online banking or an ATM. Old raw lines 18-55 restrict the captured Checkout route to one-time EUR items in payment mode and describe Europe/US business scope. Old raw lines 218-238 and 307-392 separate server creation of a EUR PaymentIntent from confirmation with the client secret and billing email, with an optional server confirmation path. Old raw lines 109-127 and 543-556 distinguish voucher creation from eventual paid status and fulfillment. source-stripe-multibanco-accept-payment.md retains the voucher fields and central lifecycle but needs to identify the distinct Checkout Session and PaymentIntent events, qualify the processing buffer, and separate mobile webview results from payment success.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/multibanco/accept-a-payment, new raw lines 5-17 are navigation to the same four query variants named in old raw lines 8-10, 193-195, 614-616 and 895-897. The capture format changed and supplies no substantive product change. Keep the detailed behavior dated 2026-05-07. Old raw lines 109-127 show that a Checkout voucher redirect or `checkout.session.completed` establishes issuance, while asynchronous success supports fulfillment. Old raw lines 350-385, 387-518, 778-805 and 1034-1078 distinguish the default Stripe.js modal, optional server redirect or manual presentation, and mobile SDK display results. Old raw lines 164-182 describe the sandbox 11-day test, seven days of voucher validity, a conditional processing interval of up to four more days, automatic refund initiation for late or canceled-voucher funds, and replacement instructions after successful reconfirmation. In source-stripe-multibanco-accept-payment.md and the voucher concept, clarify the different event families, online banking versus generic cash-only wording, and server-observed payment status versus voucher availability, live eligibility, settlement or completion of a refund.
